correctness.rationale: The full six-exception iff claim is proved by the three-new-vertex edge-subdivision lemma, a reduction of all cycle and bridge lengths to 231 base triples, and a complete finite certificate. The 225 positive triples carry explicit independently checked vertex sets. The remaining six have been exhaustively tested over every vertex subset using a separately constructed adjacency graph; the reported packing-subset counts are 22, 31, 26, 66, 97, 304 and all yield zero isolating packings. Both scripts were run from their actual package-source paths and recorded outputs reproduced. The proof handles d=0, d>=1, triangle cycles, and all cycle lengths without extrapolating from finite experiments.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating full text proves the all-tree case and identifies C5 as an obstruction, but not two-cycle cacti. The 2021 barbell connected vertex-edge domination polynomial addresses a mathematically different selected-set constraint. Exact 2-packing isolation for maximum-degree-two components does not imply gluing of two cycles through a bridge. Direct formulation, parameter, alternate terminology, stronger-coverage and related database searches found no covering result, though unindexed and inaccessible texts remain residual risks.

value.rationale: This gives a complete, natural, all-parameters classification on the basic infinite bicyclic cactus family, bridging a known all-tree guarantee and the first pentagonal failure. The precise nonmonotone bridge-length obstruction list, together with the unusual triangle–pentagon failure and the robust subdivision lemma, adds substantive structural information beyond routine isolated small examples or merely reproducing a known table.
